title: Lorenzo Tio's pupils and Wilkins's career; Peter's thrift
summary: Tats and Bocage's brother studied under Tio; the brother played with Joe Robichaux and Peter; Peter was thrifty and left two houses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Last time I saw Tats, downtown I was talking to him on Clever and in Dumain one night, and Tats told me he couldn't play no more either, because he had that stroke, you know. Yeah. But that was a good sax man too, clarinet man. Well they came underneath T.O., Lorenzi T.O. Lorenzi T.O. Lorenzi T.O. was the greatest the city had. That's where my little brother learned, under T.O.
Yeah. Well, how old is your little brother?

Well, my little brother, he was about forty-nine when he died. Mm-hmm. Oh, he played with the best of them, him. He played, he left here one time, he went with, uh, went with the Banner Band, New Ivery, stayed up there about a year. He came back and him and Freddie Coleman and, uh, went with Joe Robichaud. Well, they started traveling a while, him and Freddie, with Joe Robichaud. They went all up New York, Mexico, and all about. And all they traveling, when they got back here, they didn't have a dime. They said, uh, they had their expense, had up all the money, everything they did. And when they come back, they come back, then you had a dime. Not all the traveling they'd done. Well, then after my brother left Joe Robichaud, he started playing with Peter, according to Peter. He started playing with him. But he was, my little brother, was a first-class sax player.
Pete ought to show him how to save money, huh?
No, he never spent no money. Pete never did go nowhere. That's the trouble.

No, he, uh, Pete was a man. He didn't drink or nothing, and he didn't go out. Mostly Pete, you'd find Pete sitting on that porch up there. If I'd come outside, he'd come over here and sit down on the porch, you know, me and him, and talk. Well, he left. He sure had a little few nickels when he died. He got two houses. He's got this house. He's got another house up on Socratch Street.
